# runlab-client

> Python client and HTTP spec for the RunLab research API, for AI researchers, ML engineers
> and their coding agents: did a change actually help? Pre-register an A-vs-B comparison, record
> each seed's metric, and get a verdict. The verdict comes from a paired test with a 95 %
> confidence interval, checked against the plan. It refuses a misleading comparison and says
> which wins a write-up may quote. The client uses only the standard library. Get started:
> `pip install runlab-client`, then `runlab demo` (sign in with GitHub, then a first verdict
> on simulated numbers) or `runlab login`; `RunLab()` then needs no settings (in CI: env
> RUNLAB_TOKEN, RUNLAB_URL; in GitHub Actions, `runlab verdict` can run keyless with
> `id-token: write`).

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/omer-nachman/runlab-python/blob/main/README.md): get started (`runlab demo`), quickstart, the loop, verdict codes, studies (also `runlab worker`: seeds on your machine), errors, client reference
- [README, Pull-request check](https://github.com/omer-nachman/runlab-python/blob/main/README.md#pull-request-check-runlab-verdict): `runlab verdict`, a check that records the seeds, compares and passes or fails a pull request; the spec `.runlab/verdict.yml` is read from the base commit
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/omer-nachman/runlab-python/blob/main/AGENTS.md): how a coding agent should run the loop and report the result
- [OpenAPI 3.1 spec](https://github.com/omer-nachman/runlab-python/blob/main/openapi.json): 11 operations under /api/v1, bearer-token auth

## Examples

- [quickstart.py](https://github.com/omer-nachman/runlab-python/blob/main/examples/quickstart.py): plan, 10 seeds per arm, compare
- [curl.sh](https://github.com/omer-nachman/runlab-python/blob/main/examples/curl.sh): the same loop with curl

## Optional

- [Client source](https://github.com/omer-nachman/runlab-python/blob/main/src/runlab_client/__init__.py): about 1,500 lines in two files (`__init__.py`, `verdict.py`)
